items.title: Descent data for a family of morphisms is the same as descent data for their coproduct
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file descent.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: For a family of morphisms with target S and X the coproduct of their sources, the lemma produces a canonical equivalence between descent data relative to the family and descent data relative to the single morphism X to S, described explicitly on objects (statement lines 8466-8485). The proof is a direct unpacking: the fibre product of the coproduct with itself over S is the coproduct of the pairwise fibre products, and likewise for higher fibre products, so a morphism to X is the same as a family of morphisms to the components and a descent datum is the same as a family of comparison isomorphisms indexed by pairs (proof lines 8487-8492). The claim is H2: no construction beyond identifying the fibre products, which the author states and which is exactly the content.
